title: Full AES-256 key-structure boomerang baseline with 2^17 related-subkey oracles, GSW 2022 source conflict

target.description: Standard full AES-256: the rounds-2-to-14 boomerang distinguisher receives one prepended round for key recovery. This record selects the baseline with 2^16 encryption keys and 2^16 decryption keys, not the later 2^19-key variant.

key_budget.reported: 2^17 related keys: 2^16 encryption keys and 2^16 decryption keys
key_budget.note: Section 4.1 constructs the two oracle families, and p.20 explicitly counts 2^17 keys. This is the author's key-oracle count, not the 2^31 unordered key pairs or 2^23 eligible key quartets formed within the structures.

setting.key_relation: Related-subkey setting: vary the prescribed 16-bit difference space of the second 256-bit subkey K^1 to derive encryption keys; obtain decryption keys by adding a fixed difference to the joint state formed by the second half of K^3 and first half of K^4, then invert/extend the schedule. These are not fixed-XOR master-key oracles.
setting.key_population: No weak-key-subset precondition is stated. The structure is based on an original secret key K0, and Section 4.3 maps key-byte proposals from the different key quartets back to K0 and its related K0-prime.
setting.plaintext_model: Eight chosen-plaintext structures of 2^72 texts, each encrypted under 2^16 keys; modified ciphertexts are decrypted under the corresponding related-subkey oracles.
assumptions: The attacker can choose differences at the specified intermediate key-schedule states and access all resulting encryption/decryption oracles.
The baseline uses one key structure and eight plaintext structures, as in Algorithm 1 and its repetitions.
The time conversion assumes one AES-256 encryption/decryption is equivalent to about 2^8 memory accesses, as counted by the authors.
The full-key claim includes the authors' assertion that completion after recovering 120 key bits does not dominate; the completion algorithm is not detailed.

time.reported: Table 1 at s=0 and Section 4.3 Complexity: 2^92.5; Section 4.3 More Tradeoffs at s=0 with 2^17 keys: 2^92
time.note: Rechecked on 2026-10-10 in the official ACISP chapter. Algorithm 1 and the Complexity section give 2^92 encryption/decryption calls plus 2^99 memory accesses. At the authors' 2^8 accesses per encryption, the sum is 2^92 + 2^91, with exponent approximately 92.585; the paper summarizes it as 2^92.5. The More Tradeoffs paragraph instead prints 2^(92+s) for 2^(17-s) keys, giving 2^92 at s=0. These are distinct printed estimates; no corrected formula was obtained, so normalization remains unset.

data.reported: Table 1 at s=0 and Section 4.3 Complexity: 2^92; Section 4.3 More Tradeoffs at s=0 with 2^17 keys: 2^91
data.note: Algorithm 1 performs 2^88 encryptions and 2^88 decryptions for each plaintext structure; eight structures give 8 * (2^88 + 2^88) = 2^92 total oracle calls. The 2^91 count covers either direction alone. Table 1 and Complexity use 2^92 total; More Tradeoffs prints 2^(91+s) for the same 2^(17-s) key budget, without redefining data as one-direction-only. This field records total calls, so the latter figure cannot silently replace the algorithm count. Both printed figures remain visible and normalization stays unset.

memory.note: Table 1 at s=0 and Section 4.3 Complexity give 2^89. Algorithm 1 describes a hash table of size 2^88 containing plaintext pairs, but the paper does not define a single unit for the final memory total; no byte or block conversion is asserted.

preprocessing.note: Key-structure creation and filtering are described within the attack; no separately quantified reusable preprocessing budget is supplied.

success.description: The source targets four right quartets and recovers a120-bit vote before an unspecified full-key completion. These statements give no numerical full-key success at either s=0 endpoint. The source binomial model is recorded symbolically: its printed four-vote approximation and expected wrong-key count are already arithmetic-conflicted, and expected counts are not probabilities of a unique correct key. Existing completion and applicable time/data conflicts remain. Key-structure pair fractions are not weak-secret-key fractions. B43 adds a source-surrogate bound for no wrong120-bit candidate receiving at least four votes. It is a local voting event, unconditioned on collecting four right quartets; complete-key success remains unquantified.

review.scope: Independent source-first and endpoint review, PDF11–18: the whole-key probability is not quantified. Expected four right quartets lacks an acquisition joint law and final256-bit completion remains unspecified. Baseline's fixed-N source voting bound is local and unconditioned; no new bound is transferred to reuse without a common120-bit vote mapping across varying K0-prime. Preserve arithmetic, completion, native-unit and time/data conflicts. Targeted source review leaves the original goal gap and full-audit gates open.

PDF12 Section4.2: five2^-6 transitions in rounds2–8, conditional on the selected optimal pair class.
PDF12 Section4.2: three2^-6 transitions in rounds10–14.
PDF12–13: source2^(2*(-30-18)) for the optimal class, after the first-round condition. Not the probability of collecting four right quartets.
PDF15 StepII1: four bits from plaintext S-box compatibility plus two from key-schedule compatibility.
PDF15 StepII6: an8-bit key-schedule equality filters proposed quartets from2^65 to2^57.
PDF16 Recover the Key: the source assumes a uniform120-bit wrong proposal for its binomial expression. No independence or exact uniformity is independently established here.

PDF16: probability of exactly four votes for ONE fixed wrong120-bit candidate under the source binomial/random-proposal model. The printed approximation2^-138.5 and expected count2^-18.5 retain the existing arithmetic conflict. This is not a probability of no wrong candidates or full-key recovery.

Baseline s=0 only, within the source fixed-N binomial surrogate: N=2^88 proposals and p=2^-120 for one fixed wrong120-bit candidate. The fourth-factorial-moment bound P(Y>=4)<=C(N,4)*p^4 and a union over at most2^120 wrong candidates give error<1/6144. Thus the displayed symbolic lower bound is valid in that model without independence between different candidates. The fixed N is the source surrogate for an expected proposal count, not a proved hard cap for the actual attack. This event is not conditioned on obtaining four right quartets, is not full256-bit recovery or an actual-AES frequency, and is not propagated to encryption reuse, whose varying decryption-side shifts change K0-prime and lack a justified common120-bit vote pool. The source's printed exactly-four-vote arithmetic conflict is retained.

evidence.locator: Section 4.1 pp.11-13 and Figure 4 p.14; Section 4.3 Algorithm 1 p.15, Steps I-II pp.16-18, and Recover the Key p.18.
evidence.interpretation: The detailed attack uses related-subkey encryption and adaptive decryption, a two-family key structure, and mappings of recovered byte proposals back to the original keys. It is a full-round/full-key author claim, not merely a 13-round distinguisher or a four-key attack.

evidence.locator: Printed p.6 Table 1, first Key-Structure Boomerang row at s=0; Section 4.3 Complexity pp.18-19; More Tradeoffs p.20 at s=0.
evidence.interpretation: The 2026-10-10 PDF visual/text recheck confirms time 2^92.5 and data 2^92 in Table 1 and Complexity for 2^17 keys. Counting both query directions over eight structures independently yields 2^92 calls; adding the source's converted memory-access work gives exponent approximately 92.585, summarized as 92.5 in the paper. More Tradeoffs prints time 2^92 and data 2^91 at the same key count. This records the source inconsistency rather than a curator-issued erratum; normalized time/data remain unset.

limitations: Unreconciled time/data figures prohibit automatic resource comparisons or an unqualified best-known claim.
The separate encryption-reuse endpoint and both source formula branches are now inventoried independently; their conflicts remain unresolved.
The related-subkey access and large key budget differ materially from ordinary single-key AES and from the four-key 2009 boomerang setting.
The mapping of memory accesses to encryption equivalents is the authors' model, not a hardware-independent runtime measurement.
The source does not detail full-key completion after 120 recovered bits; no independent attack or completion-cost reproduction was performed.

field_conflicts.label: Four-vote source arithmetic
field_conflicts.description: The printed binom(2^88,4)*(2^-120)^4*(1-2^-120)^(2^88-4) has log2 approximately-132.5849625 per wrong proposal, rather than-138.5. Across2^120 proposals expected false survivors are about2^-12.5849625, not2^-18.5. This is a local source arithmetic difference; unknown dependence and full-key success remain separate.
